title: RL policy_train
description: Why policy_train owns the step. On the E6 Snowball run — 67B total / 2B active MoE, 80 H100, FSDP2, non-colocated — policy_train was 90.4% of a 4209.7 s step and was a single leaf timer. This dashboard reads the per-rank spans MarinSkyRL now publishes from inside the policy worker, picks the rank the driver actually waited for, and puts the DCGM occupancy of the same nodes beside them. Rollout is a sibling of policy_train, not a child of it, and has its own row at the bottom.

params.value: SELECT DISTINCT run_id AS value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND name = 'policy_step' AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND run_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Where the step goes — driver phases, measured on the driver
Step composition — exclusive seconds per phase
panels.description: Mean seconds each driver phase spent on its own work inside one optimizer step: the phase's wall minus the walls of the phases that name it as their parent. Exclusive time is the only kind that may be stacked, and it telescopes, so these bands sum to the step no matter how deep the tree gets. Which phases exist depends on the trainer and on the build: the synchronous trainer records no run_training, so fwd_logprobs_values_reward and train_critic_and_policy attach straight to step, and the generate subtree (rollout_collect, rollout_assemble, rollout_finalize and their children) exists only on builds that publish it. Nothing here is enumerated, so a new span appears as its own band and is subtracted from its parent's on the same day it ships. Two bands read oddly on purpose. `generate` near zero is the correct statement that generate is pure orchestration and all of its wall is in its children — it equals the published generate_span_residual, and a disagreement between them means a child row was lost in transport. `train_critic_and_policy` is the Ray dispatch and collection around policy_train, a second or two that used to be invisible. A negative band is not noise: it means a child was counted inside its parent, and it is left signed rather than clamped. Only the root='step' subtree is read — save_checkpoints, queue_hf_export and eval sit beside a step and can neither be added to nor subtracted from it.

defaults.noValue: No inclusive-wall driver rows. This build does not publish step timings to telemetry, or the selected run predates them.

params.value: WITH driver AS ( SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS bucket, json_get(attributes_json, 'step') AS s, json_get(attributes_json, 'phase') AS phase, json_get(attributes_json, 'parent') AS parent, value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND name = 'phase_duration_seconds' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'role') = 'trainer' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'clock_domain') = 'inclusive_wall' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'root') = 'step' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) ), contained AS ( SELECT bucket, s, parent AS phase, SUM(value) AS child_seconds FROM driver WHERE parent IS NOT NULL AND parent <> '' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ), banded AS ( SELECT driver.bucket AS bucket, CASE WHEN driver.phase = 'step' THEN 'unattributed' ELSE driver.phase END AS band, driver.value - COALESCE(contained.child_seconds, 0) AS seconds FROM driver LEFT JOIN contained ON contained.bucket = driver.bucket AND contained.s = driver.s AND contained.phase = driver.phase ) SELECT bucket AS t, band AS series, AVG(seconds) AS value FROM banded GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: policy_train share of the step
panels.description: policy_train as a fraction of the enclosing step, from the same driver rows as the panel to the left. This is the triage number: on E6 Snowball it reads about 0.90, which is the reason this dashboard exists — the phase that owned nine tenths of the wall clock was a single leaf timer with nothing inside it. Read low, generation owns the step instead and the generate row below is the one to open. The denominator is the published `step` span when there is one and the sum of the step's direct children otherwise, because they partition it by construction and no run has published a `step` span since the generate tree landed; a panel that insisted on the span would be permanently blank. Compare against the accelerator row — a phase this large with low SM activity is stranded GPU time, not slow arithmetic.

params.value: WITH driver AS ( SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS bucket, json_get(attributes_json, 'step') AS s, json_get(attributes_json, 'phase') AS phase, json_get(attributes_json, 'parent') AS parent, value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND name = 'phase_duration_seconds' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'role') = 'trainer' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'clock_domain') = 'inclusive_wall' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'root') = 'step' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) ), per_step AS ( SELECT bucket, s, MAX(CASE WHEN phase = 'policy_train' THEN value END) AS policy_train, COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN phase = 'step' THEN value END), SUM(CASE WHEN parent = 'step' THEN value END)) AS step_seconds FROM driver GROUP BY 1, 2 ) SELECT bucket AS t, AVG(policy_train / NULLIF(step_seconds, 0)) AS policy_train_share FROM per_step GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Inside policy_train — the critical rank the driver waited for
policy_ppo_train decomposition at the critical rank
panels.description: The exclusive worker spans inside policy_train, for r* = argmax_rank(policy_ppo_train) at each step — the rank the driver actually blocked on. Aggregating per phase across ranks would be wrong and would not merely be noisy: barrier time and compute time are ANTI-correlated across ranks, because the last rank to arrive waits about nothing in the entry barrier and then does a full compute while early ranks do the reverse. Per-phase maxima therefore come from different ranks and can sum to more than the parent. Use the skew panel to the right for spread, never this one. `unattributed` is computed here as the parent minus the bands, not read from the published policy_span_residual, and it is signed: positive means the spans miss where the time goes, negative means they double-count. That is not a hypothetical. policy_training_step wraps forward, backward, optimizer and entropy, so banding it beside them counts that time twice — on the first instrumented run it published as policy_training_step_other with clock_domain=exclusive_wall at 1705.8 s inside a 1706.2 s parent, and the producer's own residual read -1703.5 s. Both spellings are excluded by name, and once the parent is recomputed the same rows close to about -0.2 s. policy_span_publish is measured at step N and published under step N-1, so its sub-second band lands one bucket late. Step 1 is warm-up dominated -- compilation, the first unshard and the allocator caches all land in it -- so read steady state from step 2 onward and narrow the time range rather than averaging the two together. One trap to know about: on the first instrumented run, step 2 published a 37 s train_step carrying outcome=failure, because the run died mid-step. A short step is a truncated step, not a fast one -- check the outcome attribute before believing a step got faster. Measured steady state runs the other way: across three arms step 2 takes about 15% LONGER than step 1 (about 1715 s -> 1972 s), and that gap does not track token count. The worker sink stamps one of two clock domains and the choice changes what every number here means: `_wall` when trainer.policy_train_spans_synchronize is set, `_launch` when it is not, because without a device synchronise a span measures kernel launch rather than execution and charges a backward's real cost to whatever later call happens to block. The panel reads either, and a run stamps only one — but the two must never be compared or averaged together, so check which one the run published before quoting a number from here.

custom.axisLabel: mean seconds per step at r*

defaults.noValue: No worker spans. Set trainer.policy_train_spans=true and check that the telemetry endpoint, run id and execution uid reached the Ray actors — an unconfigured runtime discards every record and still reports a healthy flush.

params.value: WITH spans AS ( SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS bucket, json_get(attributes_json, 'step') AS s, json_get(attributes_json, 'rank') AS worker_rank, json_get(attributes_json, 'phase') AS phase, json_get(attributes_json, 'clock_domain') AS domain, value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND name = 'phase_duration_seconds' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'role') = 'worker' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) ), tagged AS ( SELECT bucket, s, worker_rank, phase, domain, value, FIRST_VALUE(worker_rank) OVER ( PARTITION BY s ORDER BY CASE WHEN phase = 'policy_ppo_train' AND domain IN ('inclusive_wall', 'inclusive_launch') THEN value ELSE -1 END DESC, worker_rank ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING ) AS critical_rank, MAX(CASE WHEN phase = 'policy_ppo_train' AND domain IN ('inclusive_wall', 'inclusive_launch') THEN value END) OVER (PARTITION BY s) AS parent_seconds, SUM(CASE WHEN domain IN ('exclusive_wall', 'exclusive_launch') AND phase NOT IN ('policy_training_step', 'policy_training_step_other', 'policy_span_residual') THEN value END) OVER (PARTITION BY s, worker_rank) AS covered_seconds FROM spans ), banded AS ( SELECT bucket, CASE WHEN domain IN ('inclusive_wall', 'inclusive_launch') THEN 'unattributed' ELSE phase END AS band, CASE WHEN domain IN ('inclusive_wall', 'inclusive_launch') THEN parent_seconds - covered_seconds ELSE value END AS seconds FROM tagged WHERE worker_rank = critical_rank AND ((domain IN ('exclusive_wall', 'exclusive_launch') AND phase NOT IN ('policy_training_step', 'policy_training_step_other', 'policy_span_residual')) OR (domain IN ('inclusive_wall', 'inclusive_launch') AND phase = 'policy_ppo_train')) ) SELECT bucket AS t, band AS series, AVG(seconds) AS value FROM banded GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Rank skew: policy_ppo_train across ranks
panels.description: The spread of policy_ppo_train over the ranks of one step. The gap between max and p50 is the arrival and straggler skew the driver pays for; it is the only thing the cross-rank spread may be read for. The max line is r*, whose row set the panel to the left decomposes. Do not subtract these from the driver's policy_train and call the difference driver overhead: the driver waits for the last-returning rank while this reports the longest-running one, and they need not be the same rank.

params.value: WITH ppo AS ( SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS bucket, value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND name = 'phase_duration_seconds' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'role') = 'worker' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'phase') = 'policy_ppo_train' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'clock_domain') IN ('inclusive_wall', 'inclusive_launch') AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) ) SELECT bucket AS t, MAX(value) AS slowest_rank, approx_percentile_cont(value, 0.95) AS p95, approx_percentile_cont(value, 0.50) AS p50, MIN(value) AS fastest_rank FROM ppo GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: policy_train ÷ micro-step count
panels.description: Driver policy_train divided by the number of micro-steps the workers actually ran, with the micro-step count itself on the right axis. Per-layer FSDP parameter all-gathers are paid once per micro-step, so at micro_train_batch_size_per_gpu=1 the gather count is linear in this denominator and the ratio is what says whether raising the micro-batch bought anything: a flat ratio with a halved count is a real win, an inversely proportional ratio is not. Counted from the batch rather than derived from config, so a mismatch between the two is visible.

defaults.noValue: No policy_train_count rows. The spans and these counters are published from the same block, so spans without counters means the run predates them or the batch carried no attention_mask -- it does not mean the batch was unpadded.

params.value: WITH driver AS ( SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS bucket, json_get(attributes_json, 'step') AS s, MAX(value) AS seconds FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND name = 'phase_duration_seconds' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'role') = 'trainer' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'clock_domain') = 'inclusive_wall' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'phase') = 'policy_train' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2 ), micro AS ( SELECT json_get(attributes_json, 'step') AS s, MAX(value) AS micro_steps FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND name = 'policy_train_count' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'counter') = 'micro_step_count' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1 ), joined AS ( SELECT driver.bucket AS bucket, driver.seconds AS seconds, micro.micro_steps AS micro_steps FROM driver JOIN micro ON driver.s = micro.s ) SELECT bucket AS t, AVG(seconds / NULLIF(micro_steps, 0)) AS seconds_per_micro_step, AVG(micro_steps) AS micro_steps FROM joined GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: backward ÷ forward at the critical rank
panels.description: The ratio of policy_backward to policy_forward on r*. With FSDP2 the backward pays a second parameter all-gather when reshard_after_forward is on, and gradient checkpointing adds a third for the recompute forward, so the ratio rises well above the arithmetic 2:1 when the gathers are the cost rather than the maths. Both spans are device-synchronised at their boundaries when trainer.policy_train_spans_synchronize is set, and the sink says which by stamping clock_domain=exclusive_wall; with it off they measure launch time, ship as exclusive_launch, and this ratio means something else. The panel reads either domain because a run publishes only one, but never compare a synchronised series against an unsynchronised one.

params.value: WITH spans AS ( SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS bucket, json_get(attributes_json, 'step') AS s, json_get(attributes_json, 'rank') AS worker_rank, json_get(attributes_json, 'phase') AS phase, json_get(attributes_json, 'clock_domain') AS domain, value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND name = 'phase_duration_seconds' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'role') = 'worker' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) ), tagged AS ( SELECT bucket, s, worker_rank, phase, domain, value, FIRST_VALUE(worker_rank) OVER ( PARTITION BY s ORDER BY CASE WHEN phase = 'policy_ppo_train' AND domain IN ('inclusive_wall', 'inclusive_launch') THEN value ELSE -1 END DESC, worker_rank ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING ) AS critical_rank, MAX(CASE WHEN phase = 'policy_ppo_train' AND domain IN ('inclusive_wall', 'inclusive_launch') THEN value END) OVER (PARTITION BY s) AS parent_seconds, SUM(CASE WHEN domain IN ('exclusive_wall', 'exclusive_launch') AND phase NOT IN ('policy_training_step', 'policy_training_step_other', 'policy_span_residual') THEN value END) OVER (PARTITION BY s, worker_rank) AS covered_seconds FROM spans ), per_step AS ( SELECT bucket, s, MAX(CASE WHEN phase = 'policy_forward' THEN value END) AS forward_seconds, MAX(CASE WHEN phase = 'policy_backward' THEN value END) AS backward_seconds FROM tagged WHERE worker_rank = critical_rank AND domain IN ('exclusive_wall', 'exclusive_launch') GROUP BY 1, 2 ) SELECT bucket AS t, AVG(backward_seconds / NULLIF(forward_seconds, 0)) AS backward_over_forward FROM per_step GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Waiting and collective share at the critical rank
panels.description: The share of policy_ppo_train that r* spent in a barrier or a collective rather than in forward, backward or the optimizer: policy_entry_barrier, policy_final_barrier, policy_metric_allreduce and policy_entropy_allreduce over the whole span. On r* the entry barrier is close to zero by construction — it is the last rank to arrive — so a large share here is not arrival skew but real synchronisation cost, and arrival skew belongs to the rank-skew panel instead.

params.value: WITH spans AS ( SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS bucket, json_get(attributes_json, 'step') AS s, json_get(attributes_json, 'rank') AS worker_rank, json_get(attributes_json, 'phase') AS phase, json_get(attributes_json, 'clock_domain') AS domain, value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND name = 'phase_duration_seconds' AND json_get(attributes_json, 'role') = 'worker' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) ), tagged AS ( SELECT bucket, s, worker_rank, phase, domain, value, FIRST_VALUE(worker_rank) OVER ( PARTITION BY s ORDER BY CASE WHEN phase = 'policy_ppo_train' AND domain IN ('inclusive_wall', 'inclusive_launch') THEN value ELSE -1 END DESC, worker_rank ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING ) AS critical_rank, MAX(CASE WHEN phase = 'policy_ppo_train' AND domain IN ('inclusive_wall', 'inclusive_launch') THEN value END) OVER (PARTITION BY s) AS parent_seconds, SUM(CASE WHEN domain IN ('exclusive_wall', 'exclusive_launch') AND phase NOT IN ('policy_training_step', 'policy_training_step_other', 'policy_span_residual') THEN value END) OVER (PARTITION BY s, worker_rank) AS covered_seconds FROM spans ), per_step AS ( SELECT bucket, s, SUM(CASE WHEN phase IN ('policy_entry_barrier', 'policy_final_barrier', 'policy_metric_allreduce', 'policy_entropy_allreduce') THEN value END) AS waiting_seconds, MAX(parent_seconds) AS total_seconds FROM tagged WHERE worker_rank = critical_rank AND domain IN ('exclusive_wall', 'exclusive_launch') GROUP BY 1, 2 ) SELECT bucket AS t, AVG(COALESCE(waiting_seconds, 0) / NULLIF(total_seconds, 0)) AS waiting_share FROM per_step GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Padding waste and attention work
panels.description: Left axis: the fraction of the trained batch that is padding, one minus real tokens over padded tokens. Right axis: the attention-work proxy B·S² ÷ ΣLᵢ², the factor by which eager attention's quadratic cost exceeds what the real sequence lengths would need. Packing is rejected for Grug, so batches are BSHD-padded, and eager attention is quadratic on the padded shape — which is why the linear padded fraction understates the cost and both lines have to be read together. The ratio is computed per rank and then averaged, so it is unaffected by how the batch is sharded.

defaults.noValue: No policy_train_count rows. The spans and these counters are published from the same block, so spans without counters means the run predates them or the batch carried no attention_mask -- it does not mean the batch was unpadded.

params.value: WITH counters AS ( SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS bucket, json_get(attributes_json, 'step') AS s, json_get(attributes_json, 'rank') AS worker_rank, json_get(attributes_json, 'counter') AS counter, value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND name = 'policy_train_count' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) ), per_rank AS ( SELECT bucket, s, worker_rank, MAX(CASE WHEN counter = 'tokens_real' THEN value END) AS tokens_real, MAX(CASE WHEN counter = 'tokens_padded' THEN value END) AS tokens_padded, MAX(CASE WHEN counter = 'attention_work_ratio' THEN value END) AS attention_work FROM counters GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ) SELECT bucket AS t, AVG(1.0 - tokens_real / NULLIF(tokens_padded, 0)) AS padded_fraction, AVG(attention_work) AS attention_work_ratio FROM per_rank GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: What the accelerators were doing — DCGM, joined through the run's nodes
SM and tensor-pipe activity on this run's nodes
panels.description: DCGM SM-active and tensor-pipe-active on the GPUs of the nodes this run occupied. This is the direct test of the leading hypothesis for policy_train: that the eager 256-expert MoE loop is launch- and occupancy-bound rather than FLOP-bound. SM-active counts time with at least one warp resident, so it stays high while the device is busy doing very little; tensor-active near zero underneath a high SM-active is the signature. Read it beside the decomposition panel above. The node agent stamps no run_id and never will, so each node is credited to whichever run reported most from it in that bucket, and a node two runs share goes entirely to one of them — this is never a per-rank attribution.

defaults.noValue: No node join. Trainer rows carry no node_name, or the node agent is not reporting this cluster. This is never “the GPUs were idle”.

params.value: WITH gpu AS ( SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') AS cl, date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS bucket, node_name AS node, json_get(attributes_json, 'gpu_uuid') AS gpu_uuid, name, AVG(value) AS rate, MAX(value) AS peak, MIN(value) AS first_value, MAX(value) AS last_value FROM "telemetry_v1.node_agent" WHERE name IN ('gpu_sm_active_ratio', 'gpu_tensor_active_ratio') AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 ), run_node AS ( SELECT cl, bucket, node, run FROM ( SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') AS cl, date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS bucket, node_name AS node, run_id AS run, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( PARTITION BY COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin'), date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)), node_name ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC ) AS rn FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE node_name IS NOT NULL AND node_name <> '' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4 ) WHERE rn = 1 ) SELECT gpu.bucket AS t, CASE gpu.name WHEN 'gpu_sm_active_ratio' THEN 'SM active' ELSE 'tensor pipe active' END AS series, AVG(gpu.rate) * 100.0 AS value FROM gpu JOIN run_node ON gpu.cl = run_node.cl AND gpu.bucket = run_node.bucket AND gpu.node = run_node.node GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: GPU memory in use on this run's nodes
panels.description: DCGM framebuffer bytes in use, mean and peak across the run's GPUs. Eager attention materialises a full FP32 score tensor over the padded shape, and the headroom it leaves is what pins micro_train_batch_size_per_gpu to 1. The peak line is the number that decides whether a larger micro-batch fits with production margin; the mean is not.

params.value: WITH gpu AS ( SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') AS cl, date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS bucket, node_name AS node, json_get(attributes_json, 'gpu_uuid') AS gpu_uuid, name, AVG(value) AS rate, MAX(value) AS peak, MIN(value) AS first_value, MAX(value) AS last_value FROM "telemetry_v1.node_agent" WHERE name IN ('gpu_memory_used_bytes') AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 ), run_node AS ( SELECT cl, bucket, node, run FROM ( SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') AS cl, date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)) AS bucket, node_name AS node, run_id AS run, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( PARTITION BY COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin'), date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', to_timestamp_millis(timestamp_ms)), node_name ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC ) AS rn FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE node_name IS NOT NULL AND node_name <> '' AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4 ) WHERE rn = 1 ) SELECT gpu.bucket AS t, AVG(gpu.rate) AS mean_used_bytes, MAX(gpu.peak) AS peak_used_bytes FROM gpu JOIN run_node ON gpu.cl = run_node.cl AND gpu.bucket = run_node.bucket AND gpu.node = run_node.node GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: NVLink against PCIe receive traffic
panels.description: DCGM NVLink and PCIe throughput per direction, summed over the run's GPUs. This is the observable proxy for where the FSDP parameter all-gather goes: NVLink carries traffic that stayed inside a tray, PCIe carries what left it for the host and the network. With fsdp_size=-1 the shard group spans every rank, so a gather that crosses the tray boundary shows here as PCIe volume rising with NVLink rather than instead of it. It does not identify the fabric beyond the host — that needs NCCL_DEBUG transport lines, which nothing in the launcher currently pins or records.

panels.title: Link faults and power on this run's GPUs
panels.description: Per GPU over the selected window: peak board power, and the increase in the NVLink and PCIe error counters. Power is a gauge and is reported as a peak; the two error columns are cumulative snapshots and are reported as differences with resets discarded, which is why they are separate columns rather than separate series in one plot. A degraded link shows up as a nonzero increase here while NVLink throughput on the panel to the left stays flat. An empty table is the healthy result.

panels.title: Rollout — a sibling phase of policy_train, never inside it (trainer.py:621 generate, trainer.py:1957 policy_train)
Generated tokens per request
panels.description: The distribution of generated tokens per rollout request, from the vLLM histogram. The step cannot end until the slowest sample finishes, so the p99 over p50 gap — not the mean — is what generation costs the step. This series has been flowing for the whole life of the fleet and has never been analysed; it needs no new instrumentation. These are Prometheus-imported cumulative counters, differenced per full series identity with resets discarded, and must never be plotted beside a native Rigging counter, which is already a delta.

panels.title: Engine queue depth and why requests are waiting
panels.description: Mean queue depth per engine, and the mean number of requests held back by each reason. Both are gauges and are averaged across engines rather than summed, so the lines answer “is one engine under-subscribed” rather than “how much work is in flight”. A queue that never fills while the step waits on generation is the under-subscription signature; requests waiting on KV-cache capacity instead is the opposite problem and takes a different fix.
